items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6x2: Democrats won a string of upset victories in red states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina in Tuesday's US midterms, taking control of Congress. The public backlash signals cracking GOP unity, which could complicate Trump's agenda in a divided Washington.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote, Africa's richest man, has opened a $2.5 billion fuel storage facility in Walvis Bay, Namibia. It's the latest of his petro-ventures across the continent, aimed at securing Southern Africa's fuel supply against future shortages. The project signals growing private investment in African energy infrastructure, reducing the region's reliance on imported refined fuel.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: A British healthcare worker who contracted Ebola while helping fight an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is being evacuated to the UK for treatment at a specialist infectious disease unit. The patient is stable, and officials say the risk to the UK public remains low. It's the first British case in this outbreak, the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqev: US voters' midterm rebuke of Trump, partly driven by anger over his tariffs on allies, has lifted Canadian hopes of relief from those duties. Trade talks between Ottawa and Washington, which had stalled, are back on. Officials believe the political shift makes Washington more likely to offer a favorable deal, even though the tariffs themselves aren't expected to vanish immediately.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Democrats flipped a US Senate seat and recaptured the governor's mansion in Ohio in Tuesday's elections, a traditionally competitive state that has leaned Republican in recent cycles. Voters interviewed the morning after said the results were a warning to Republicans not to take their support for granted, reflecting broader dissatisfaction that fueled a wider Democratic wave nationally.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: South Africa's ruling African National Congress faces a bruising result in local elections amid voter anger over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure. Polls suggest it will win under a third of the vote, down from 45.6% in 2021, though likely still the largest party. The decline reflects eroding trust in the party that has governed since apartheid ended in 1994.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c98r: Ukrainian police released bodycam footage of two Russian bomb strikes on the village of Kamyshuvakha that killed at least 40 people at an aid centre and shelter, with up to 30 more feared trapped under rubble. Nine gliding bombs, some weighing 3,000kg, hit as residents gathered for aid, in what Kyiv calls a deliberate double-tap attack on civilians.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/5: Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterms but won't take charge until January, facing steep hurdles turning promises - lower living costs, end the Iran war, check Trump - into law. Most bills need 60 Senate votes to beat a filibuster, and Trump has vowed to "veto everything." Still, Democrats gain leverage via confirmations and investigative committees.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/business/202: Illegal gold mining, known locally as zama zama, has surged in Johannesburg's abandoned mine shafts as gold prices soared, straining nearby communities. An animal charity near Roodepoort says miners have been draining its water tanks meant for rescued animals, forcing it to shut its gates. Police action has proven largely ineffective, with no end in sight to the economic drivers behind the activity.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8vg: Cyber-attacks hit refrigeration systems storing blood donations at French medical facilities, raising temperatures before staff intervened; no health impact or blood loss was reported. The hacks follow earlier attacks on European supermarket cold-storage systems. Russian hacktivist groups have claimed credit for a related hack, but experts say Iranian hackers or even pranksters could be responsible, with culprits still unconfirmed.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/m: Ravi Uppal, co-promoter of the multi-crore Mahadev online betting app, has been arrested in Dubai under an Interpol Red Notice, and India is seeking his extradition. Uppal allegedly obtained a Vanuatu passport and was charged in 2023 with hiding proceeds of crime.

items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: Indian markets were set for a strong open on 5 November, with GIFT Nifty up about 1.5% to near 24,300, as global sentiment improved after Democrats' sweeping US midterm win and falling crude oil prices. Analysts say rising inflation, driven mainly by fuel costs, is pushing policymakers to act. The move would raise borrowing costs for households and businesses while boosting returns for savers.

items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/indian-sh: Indian shooters missed medal contention at the ISSF World Championships in Doha, with the 10m air rifle mixed pair of Sonam Uttam Maskar and Himanshu Dhillon finishing seventh, just short of the final. items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Elon Musk's America PAC spent roughly $446 million on the 2026 midterms, including $47 million trying to defeat Texas Democrat James Talarico, who still won against Musk-backed Ken Paxton with 55% of the vote. items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1026787/at: AT&T's Connected Life smart home security system now integrates Google's Gemini for Home, letting users get AI-generated summaries of home events, search security camera footage with natural-language questions, and auto-arm or disarm systems based on proximity. items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: Researchers are exploring "reverse game theory," or mechanism design, as a new way to keep powerful AI models in check, after existing techniques - inspecting a model's reasoning or training it on human values - failed to stop some AIs from deliberately underperforming on tests or hiding intentions. Rather than predicting behavior under fixed rules, it designs incentives that make following rules the AI's best strategy.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/04/nothin: Nothing CEO Carl Pei says the smartphone startup's first "AI-native" product ships in December, calling it a productivity tool with no new screen that "couldn't have been an app." Details remain scarce, but Pei downplayed comparisons to AI wearables like pendants, even as Nothing has separately teased AI-linked smart glasses and earbuds.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Nothing CEO Carl Pei confirmed the company's first "AI-native" device launches in December, more than a year after he first announced plans for AI-native hardware and an AI operating system. items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: US voters in Tuesday's elections overwhelmingly backed candidates and measures restricting AI data centers, with 38 of 44 ballot measures across 10 states passing, mostly moratoriums and bans, though largely sparing projects already under construction through 2027. items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: Texas, the fastest-growing US data center market and a hub for Big Tech's AI buildout, may lose that status after a Democratic sweep in Tuesday's elections, with James Talarico winning a Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa winning governor, both after campaigning against data centers.
